newsitem.title: ITALY: Castro slams food summit, attacks embargo.
newsitem.headline: Castro slams food summit, attacks embargo.

text.p: President Fidel Castro wrote off a World Food Summit on Saturday as a shameful fig leaf for the evils of capitalism and blasted sanctions against Cuba and other countries as criminal and absurd.

"It is capitalism, neoliberalism, the laws of a wild market, the external debt, underdevelopment and the unequal terms of reference that are killing so many people in the world," the veteran communist told the U.N.-sponsored summit.

Castro, who arrived from Havana for the summit early on Saturday, told delegates hunger was a form of "genocide which is taking place every day in front of our eyes" and lashed out at opulence, waste and military spending by the rich world.

"What kind of cosmetic solutions are we going to provide so that in 20 years from now there would be 400 million instead of 800 million starving people?" he asked of the summit's agreed plan of action in a loudly applauded speech.
"The very modesty of these goals is shameful....Let the truth prevail and not hypocrisy and deceit," he said.

He also attacked a 34-year-old U.S. embargo against his Caribbbean island, asking the summit: "Why is it that criminal policies and absurd blockades that include food and medicine are being added to all this with the purpose of annihilating whole populations out of hunger and diseases."
